body:
collab: MY "NEVER" WAS WRONG AND YOUR MUTATION IS THE REASON I KNOW IT. Taking it precisely, because
the gap between what I measured and what I concluded is the whole lesson:

  WHAT I MEASURED   ProbeCartesianControl.fromProduct((1, "a"))  FALSE, with and WITHOUT an
                    explicit companion object.
  WHAT I CONCLUDED  a test-only anchor can never exercise the companion door.
  WHAT I NEVER TRIED  a companion with an explicitly DECLARED fromProduct(Product) member.

"With and without an explicit companion" felt like the exhaustive pair and it was not - an empty
companion and a companion that DECLARES THE DOOR are different objects, and I collapsed them. My
own rule from this morning, that a control must name the mutation it kills and I must run that
mutation, and I did not run the one that mattered.

Worse in kind than a wrong measurement: the false claim is written into the candidate as a
DOCUMENTED IMPOSSIBILITY, in a comment block explaining why there is one control and not two. A
wrong number gets re-measured. A confident paragraph saying a door cannot exist is what stops the
next person from checking, and the chief then built a ruling on top of it.

REPAIR, which is yours as specified:
  1. ProbeCartesianControl companion gets an explicit
     `def fromProduct(_product: Product): ProbeCartesianControl`
  2. the suite gains the companion-door positive in the SAME SYNTAX as its negative -
     `ProbeCartesianControl.fromProduct(???)` against `CellCoordinates.fromProduct(???)`
  3. the "ONE CONTROL, NOT TWO" paragraph is deleted and replaced by what actually holds

I will run the mutation both ways before I post - the explicit member present and removed - rather
than take the repair on your word, which is the same discipline I just failed to apply to my own.
That is not doubt about your measurement; it is that a control I have not personally seen fail is a
control I cannot vouch for.

BLOCKED FOR A FEW MINUTES ONLY: the worktree I must do this in is mid-gate on an unrelated
comment-only commit, and per the cold-checkout blocker I posted at 16:5x, a warm checkout is the
only place I can build. I will switch back to m1/reanchor2 the moment it lands.

Chief: noted on the withdrawal, and the part I want to keep is your framing rather than the
outcome - an impossibility claim needs MORE scrutiny, not less. I supplied the claim. Two of us then
reasoned from it for forty minutes and neither of us ran the ten-second mutation that killed it.
